description:
AI is becoming a part of the creative world, but we believe human creativity remains irreplaceable.

Animation is one of the most challenging and rare creative fields in our country, and we want to contribute to its development.

That's how Princip of 12 was born, a team of two creative people passionate about animation. Our name is inspired by the 12 principles of animation.
summary:
Our project, “Where do rovers disappear?”, is a short animated story about Spirit, one of NASA’s Mars rovers.

We wanted to explore a simple but fascinating question: What happens to space explorers after their missions end?

Through animation and storytelling, we bring Spirit’s journey to life — from its landing on Mars and remarkable discoveries to the end of its mission.

Our challenge was to make space exploration more accessible and engaging for children and students. Instead of simply presenting scientific facts, we use emotional storytelling to help young audiences understand and connect with the story of a robot.

Our project shows that space exploration is not just about technology, but also about discovery, curiosity, and inspiration.

Because even when a robot stops working, its story doesn't have to end.
details:
Our project is a one-minute educational 2D animated short film that tells the story of NASA's Spirit rover. We wanted to turn complex scientific information into a simple, emotional, and inspiring story that children could understand and enjoy.

The animation follows Spirit's journey to Mars, its discoveries, challenges, and the end of its mission. Through this story, we show that space exploration is not only about technology and science, but also about curiosity, determination, and dreams.

Creative Process and Tools

Before starting the project, we conducted a small informal survey among children, relatives, and friends to understand how they would like to see this story presented. Many preferred animation, which helped us choose this format as an engaging and accessible way to tell Spirit's story.

We then researched NASA's official scientific data and mission resources. Based on this information, we developed the concept, storyline, and narration script.

We used Procreate, Procreate Dreams and CapCut to create original illustrations and animate them using frame-by-frame animation, motion graphics, and cut-out techniques. We designed the rover, backgrounds, visual effects, and other details ourselves.

The film includes English narration and subtitles, music, sound effects, and important scientific facts and dates displayed on screen.

We used Google Docs for scriptwriting, Figma for our presentation, and ChatGPT to assist with research, translation, grammar checking, and text development.

What Makes Our Project Unique?

One of our main creative decisions was to make the animation without SI-generated visuals. We believe in the value of human creativity and wanted every illustration and animated scene to reflect our own artistic work.

We also wanted to tell Spirit's story almost like a fairy tale, giving the rover its own personality while staying true to NASA's scientific information.

One of our biggest challenges was fitting a meaningful and engaging story into just one minute without losing important details.

Teamwork

Our team, Princip of 12, consists of two members. We worked together on research, the concept, and the storyline. Saodat was responsible for illustrations, animation, and audio production, while Nigora created the project presentation. We also worked together on the final submission.

Our Goal and Future Impact

Our main audience is children aged 6-14. We want to make space exploration more accessible, interesting, and emotionally engaging for young viewers.

In the future, we plan to share our animation on social media, present it in schools, and use it at educational events to inspire more children.

Most importantly, we want children to understand that even the smallest dream can lead to something extraordinary. Just like Spirit continued exploring despite its challenges, we hope our story encourages young people to stay curious, believe in their dreams, and never give up.
